absent: Locking semantics of the real mode stack loader and any multiprocessor exclusion during trampoline execution.
Layout and initialization of shared trampoline slots for target address, descriptor pointers, control images, flags and paging depth.
Numeric values of segment selectors, control word images, MSR identifiers and descriptor table contents.
Behavior of processor verification, display probe and mode set, default port setup and delay helpers.
Format of trampoline page tables and 64-bit descriptor tables.
Action after signature failure beyond diverting to an unshown error label.
Firmware contract and side effects of the fixed BIOS far call during resume.
Value and generation of the real mode end integrity signature.

findings.text: The real mode image exports base marker pa_real_mode_base with entry pa_text_start and read only end pa_ro_end plus a handler table bounded by video_cards and video_cards_end, execution begins at the text entry while the segment base stays at zero.

Layout places a header at offset zero, then word aligned read data holding a sixteen byte aligned video table, then page aligned code for real plus 32-bit plus 64-bit stages, then page aligned writable data, then 128 byte aligned uninitialized storage with a word aligned integrity signature at the end, discarding note and debug sections and pulling in generated symbols.

Entry machine_real_restart_asm drives return toward real mode, on 64-bit builds first adopting a trampoline table below four gigabytes and disabling paging to leave long mode before clearing extended features at a paging off continuation, then on all builds loading a real mode interrupt table with a temporary descriptor table, filling data segments with sixteen bit compatible values and taking a far transfer onward.

The 32-bit secondary processor path writes back caches, resynchronizes execution, adopts code as data, blocks interrupts, fetches onward address from shared storage tr_start, installs a null interrupt table with a supplied descriptor table using wide loads for high addresses, enables protection and far jumps to protected starter pa_startup_32 under the boot selector.
Protected starter startup_32 forwards indirectly through the previously loaded general register to a kernel supplied continuation, shared by the 32-bit trampoline chain and the suspend resume chain.

The 64-bit secondary path blocks interrupts and writes back caches, resynchronizes, derives data segments from code, loads a locked real mode stack, verifies long mode support and halts on failure, otherwise installs null interrupt with supplied descriptor tables via wide loads, enters protected mode without paging and far jumps to the protected starter.

Confidential guest entry sev_es_trampoline_start repeats early interrupt block with resynchronization plus segment setup plus locked stack load, then jumps directly to the shared protected switch, omitting cache writeback and processor verification.

Protected stage startup_32 reloads segments from a passed selector and biases stack by the real base, conditionally sets the memory encryption enable in system configuration when activity flag TH_FLAGS_SME_ACTIVE_BIT indicates need, restores saved pa_tr_cr4 and trampoline top table pa_trampoline_pgd, converges extended features toward pa_tr_efer while skipping redundant writes to avoid guest exceptions, then enables paging for long mode and far jumps to startup_64 under the kernel selector.

Direct 64-bit entry trampoline_start64 loads null interrupt with 64-bit descriptor tables, compares current paging depth against desired tr_cr4 for the five level indicator and either continues in 64-bit mode by loading a locked stack plus reloading segments plus installing the trampoline top table before far returning to virtual target tr_start, or diverts via trampoline selector tr_compat to helper pa_trampoline_compat which prepares stack and selector, disables paging and reenters the protected starter to toggle paging depth.
Starter startup_64 performs a single indirect jump to the kernel virtual address held in shared storage, completing the transition from identity mapped trampoline to paged kernel execution.

The resume header is packed without padding. It starts with 16-bit video_mode, then 32-bit pmode_entry alongside 16-bit pmode_cs, then 32-bit pmode_cr0 plus 32-bit pmode_cr3 and 32-bit pmode_cr4, then 32-bit pmode_efer_low plus 32-bit pmode_efer_high alongside 64-bit pmode_gdt, then 32-bit pmode_misc_en_low plus 32-bit pmode_misc_en_high, then 32-bit pmode_behavior plus 32-bit realmode_flags plus 32-bit real_magic ending with 32-bit signature.

WAKEUP_HEADER_OFFSET denotes header distance eight from image base with WAKEUP_HEADER_SIGNATURE denoting expected value 0x51ee1111, while restore control places WAKEUP_BEHAVIOR_RESTORE_MISC_ENABLE at bit zero plus WAKEUP_BEHAVIOR_RESTORE_CR4 at bit one plus WAKEUP_BEHAVIOR_RESTORE_EFER at bit two.

DOT_HZ denotes dot tone 880 hertz with DASH_HZ denoting dash tone 587 hertz and US_PER_DOT denoting dot length 125000 microseconds, resume magic real_magic expects 0x12345678, and realmode_flags uses bit zero for a fixed BIOS call plus bit one for display probe and mode set plus value four for an audible test pattern.

Wake entry wakeup_start disables interrupts and string direction, resynchronizes, repairs possibly corrupt segment caches by a brief protected excursion that reloads all data segments before returning to real mode, establishes stack and segments from code, installs its private interrupt table, clears flags and checks both header signature and end signature before calling C main, diverting to an error label on mismatch.

After the C call the resume flow conditionally restores machine specific enable per behavior bit zero, then on 32-bit builds always restores translation base while restoring extended control and extended features only per their behavior bits, loads saved descriptor pointer pmode_gdt, restores saved protection control pmode_cr0 and far jumps through the protected starter to saved address pmode_entry, while 64-bit builds transfer to the 64-bit trampoline entry.

C routine main installs default port operations via pio_ops, spins forever on magic mismatch, emits a fixed audible pattern when the test flag is present, issues a fixed BIOS far call when the BIOS flag is present, and when the video flag is present probes display adapters without state preservation then applies header video_mode.

Morse helper send_morse walks a null terminated pattern, sounding a dot as one interval tone plus one interval silence and a dash as triple interval tone plus single silence with any other character as triple silence, silencing the speaker after each sounded element.

Speaker helper beep derives divisor from base 1193181 divided by requested frequency, writes control value 0xb6 to port 0x43 then low and high divisor bytes to port 0x42 with delays, performs a dummy read of port 0x61 and gates output through the same port using 0x03 for sound and 0x00 for silence.

Several failures are terminal, magic mismatch spins forever, header or end signature mismatch diverts to an error label, failed long mode verification halts in a loop, and any fault under a null interrupt table shuts the processor down instead of returning to firmware.

Transitions block interrupts early and write back caches for multi socket safety, use wide descriptor loads to reach tables beyond sixteen megabytes, keep the reboot trampoline table below four gigabytes, preserve segment bases across mode changes and skip redundant extended feature writes that would fault in confidential guests.

Cross file symbols shared within the dossier include protected starter startup_32 reused by resume, 64-bit trampoline reused by 64-bit resume, helper pa_trampoline_compat for paging switches, direct entry trampoline_start64 for firmware handoff, plus table pio_ops with routines main and send_morse and beep.
